Modified assessment incorporating SLOOS:

- Macro and policy: The Fed held the target range at 5.25–5.50% and continued QT, acknowledging strong Q3 growth, still-low unemployment, and elevated inflation.
- SLOOS lens (credit supply and demand): The latest SLOOS shows broad-based tightening in lending standards and weaker loan demand:
  - C&I: Tighter standards for firms of all sizes; weaker demand. Drivers include economic outlook, reduced risk tolerance, funding costs, deposit outflows, liquidity positions, and mark-to-market pressures on securities.
  - CRE: Continued tightening across property types with weaker demand; concerns about collateral values and loan saleability.
  - Residential real estate: Standards tightened across mortgage categories (GSE-eligible, non-GSE, jumbo, non-QM, government); demand remained weak.
  - Consumer credit: Further tightening in credit cards and auto loans, wider loan rate spreads, lower approval likelihood for lower FICO tiers; weaker demand for auto and other consumer loans.
  - Forward-looking: Many banks anticipate further tightening over the next six months.
- Policy/market implications: SLOOS corroborates the statement’s warning that tighter credit will weigh on activity and hiring. Intensifying credit headwinds, combined with higher-for-longer rates, tilt risks to the downside for growth even as they support disinflation over time.

Overall read: Cautious-to-negative. Strong near-term activity is offset by pronounced and broad credit tightening in SLOOS, warranting a more guarded stance than a neutral read.
